content: SIMCOR tablets are a combination medication that includes niacin in an extended-release form (NIASPAN) and simvastatin. Simvastatin functions as an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, while niacin is a lipid-modifying agent. Niacin, also known as nicotinic acid or 3-pyridinecarboxylic acid, is a white, crystalline powder that does not absorb moisture from the air (nonhygroscopic). It is highly soluble in water, boiling ethanol, and propylene glycol, but it is insoluble in ethyl ether. The chemical formula for niacin is C6H5NO2, and its molecular weight is 123.11. Simvastatin is chemically described as butanoic acid, 2,2-dimethyl-, 1,2,3,7,8,8a-hexahydro-3,7-dimethyl-8-(1-naphthalenyl) ester. It appears as a white to off-white crystalline powder that is also nonhygroscopic. Simvastatin is practically insoluble in water but dissolves freely in chloroform, methanol, and ethanol. Its chemical formula is C25H38O5, and its molecular weight is 418.57. SIMCOR is formulated for oral administration and is available in the following strengths: 500 mg of niacin extended-release (NIASPAN) combined with 20 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 500/20 mg) 500 mg of niacin extended-release (NIASPAN) combined with 40 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 500/40 mg) 750 mg of niacin extended-release (NIASPAN) combined with 20 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 750/20 mg) 1000 mg of niacin extended-release (NIASPAN) combined with 20 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 1000/20 mg) 1000 mg of niacin extended-release (NIASPAN) combined with 40 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 1000/40 mg) Each SIMCOR tablet contains the following inactive ingredients: hypromellose, povidone, stearic acid, polyethylene glycol, butylated hydroxyanisole, FD&C Blue 2, lactose monohydrate, titanium dioxide, and triacetin. Additionally, the SIMCOR 500/20 mg, SIMCOR 750/20 mg, and SIMCOR 1000/20 mg formulations include iron oxide.
